Hi Garvit, (cc'ing mailing list)

You can also execute whole scripts, either using the javax.script API or the command line tool.

Here's a link on how to do it with the javax.script API:
http://docs.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/technotes/guides/scripting/programmer_guide/#evalfile

And you can run scripts using the renjin command line tool: (IIRC)
renjin -f myscript.R

Of course, all pull requests are very much welcome!! (We've got a rather long to-do list :-)

Best,
Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Regarding Renjin
parts:
Hi Garvit,

You can use (most) of the normal R functions to read data files such as read.table() or read.csv() or load() for objects serialized in R's own serialization format. You can also use Renjin's internal Java API for serialized files: see RDataReader and RDataWriter.

You can find documentation on renjin.org but I fear the quality and completeness is presently not great, but it should give you a few pointers to get started.

Best,
Alex

I'm not sure what a SisuIndexAPT6 is, but apparently it doesn't support java 1.7 (Java 7) and you've compiled your program for Java 7. You can tell javac to generate Java 6 code by providing the argument -target 1.6.

Hope this helps!
